subject: sentences
title: What does it mean?
about: Working out a new word from the sentences around it (Ben was drowsy, he yawned and went to bed), reading a word that has two meanings (bat, bark, trunk, watch) the right way for its sentence, and using the word parts re- and un-. This is NC L.1.4, the first-grade standard for unknown and multiple-meaning words, using context clues and word parts.
tip: Before he taps, ask what clue told him; the clue is always in the sentence next to the new word.

cards.q: Ben was drowsy. He yawned and went to bed. Drowsy means...
cards.note: The clues are yawned and went to bed. Drowsy means sleepy.

cards.q: Mia's hands were chilly. She put on her mittens. What does chilly mean?
cards.note: Mittens keep hands warm, so chilly must mean cold.

cards.q: The dog gobbled his food. It was gone in a flash! Gobbled means...
cards.note: Gone in a flash is the clue. Gobbled means ate very fast.

cards.q: Sam was glum. He lost his best ball. What does glum mean?
cards.note: He lost his ball, so he feels sad. Glum means sad.

cards.q: Zoe was thrilled. She got a new bike! Another word for thrilled is...
cards.note: A new bike is a happy thing. Thrilled means very, very happy.

cards.q: The old bridge was wobbly. It shook when we walked on it. What does wobbly mean?
cards.note: It shook is the clue. Wobbly means shaky.

cards.q: Max was famished. He ate two big bowls of rice! Famished means...
cards.note: Two big bowls is the clue. Famished means very hungry.

cards.q: The kitten was timid. It hid under the chair. Timid means...
cards.note: It hid is the clue. Timid means shy.

cards.q: A bat flew out of the cave at night. Here, bat means...
cards.note: Bat has two meanings: a flying animal and a stick you hit a ball with. Flew tells us which one.

cards.q: Liv hit the ball with her bat. Here, bat means...
cards.note: Hit the ball tells us this bat is the stick, not the animal.

cards.q: The dog gave a loud bark at the door. In this sentence, bark means...
cards.note: Bark can be a dog's sound or the skin of a tree. The dog tells us which one.

cards.q: The bark on the old oak tree is rough. In this sentence, bark means...
cards.note: On the tree tells us this bark is the tree's skin.

cards.q: The elephant lifts hay with its trunk. Here, trunk means...
cards.note: Trunk can be an elephant's nose, the thick part of a tree, or a big box. Lifts hay tells us it is the nose.

cards.q: Dad looked at his watch. It was time for lunch. Here, watch means...
cards.note: Watch can mean to look at something, or a little clock on your arm. Time for lunch is the clue.

cards.q: Max had to redo his drawing. Another word for redo is...
cards.note: Re at the start of a word means again. Redo is do again.

cards.q: Zoe will refill her cup with water. What does refill mean?
cards.note: Re means again. Refill is fill again.

cards.q: Liv was unhappy about the rain. Which words mean the same as unhappy?
cards.note: Un at the start of a word means not. Unhappy is not happy.
